# landing/ — marketing page

A static page: React 18 UMD with in-browser Babel, and no build step. Preview it with the `landing` entry in `.claude/launch.json`.

- **Every claim must match what the code does today.** Don't add accuracy, latency or throughput figures, and don't describe a live mode as shipped. The owner chose facts over marketing numbers.
- **`app/data.js` is real pipeline data.** `export_data.py` generates it; run `ai/.venv/bin/python landing/export_data.py` from the repo root. Never hand-edit it. It holds keypoints only and no video frames, because the fight footage isn't ours to publish.
- **Red and blue always mean corners, and orange is only the brand and CTA colour**, so a strike mark never reads as a corner. Corner blue here is `#4f93ea`, not the app's `#60a5fa`, because the lighter blue fails the dataviz lightness band on this dark surface.
- **Upload is admin-only in the backend**, so the page's only call to action is signing in, not uploading.
- **Each scroll moves exactly one section.** With a mouse, trackpad or keyboard, `app/pager.js` handles it and CSS snapping stays off. On touch screens, native mandatory snapping handles it. Both read their stops from each element's `scroll-snap-align` in `app/site.css`, so a new section needs one; without it, both paths jump straight past the section.
- **Analytics is Umami Cloud's free plan and must stay cookieless.** The owner won't show a consent banner, so never add GA, Clarity, session replay or anything else that sets cookies. Each stored event property counts against the monthly event cap, so keep properties to one per event. The website ID is in `index.html`, and the script doesn't load on localhost.

input.recap: Fixed the hero replay in landing/app/stage.jsx: fighters keep every limb through to the end, and the head circle no longer pulses. I checked rendered frames across the whole loop and the Pose layer, with no console errors. Nothing is committed.

content.text:
I've fixed all three problems in the hero replay (the "first animation"). Both changes are in [stage.jsx](landing/app/stage.jsx). I checked frames from the start, middle and end of the loop, plus the Pose layer, and there are no console errors. Nothing is committed.

**What was wrong:** the drawing code skips any bone whose joint the pose model is less than 30% sure of.
- **Blue's leg:** the model has no detection of blue in 7 of the last 8 samples, and the one it does have places the leg joints badly. So the leg vanished and the pose froze at the end.
- **Red's left hand:** red's left elbow and wrist keep dropping below the 30% cutoff, especially near the end.
- **Red's head:** the head circle's size came from shoulder width in each frame. When a fighter turns side-on, that width shrinks from about 100 px to 5 px, so the head grew and shrank. Its centre also jumped whenever a face point crossed the cutoff.

**What changed:**
- **The loop now ends at the last sample where both fighters are detected** (sample 102 of 110). Every strike in the clip happens before that, so none are lost. Because of this, I changed the caption from "4.4 seconds" to "3.7 seconds" so it matches what plays.
- **Missing limb joints are filled in:** when the model loses an elbow, wrist, knee or ankle for up to 1 second, the joint stays attached to its parent joint. Its angle and length are blended from the frames on either side of the gap, so a limb stays the right length and doesn't fly off. This also fills red's ankles at the start of the loop, which are cut off by the edge of the broadcast frame.
- **The head size now comes from torso length,** which doesn't shrink when a fighter turns. I smoothed it over time, and the head centre now weights each face point by how sure the model is of it, so it no longer jumps.
- **The Pose layer still shows the model's own uncertainty:** its "hollow points are unsure joints" view uses the unfilled data, so the filled-in joints don't hide it.

One leftover that comes from the data itself: during blue's middle kick (around sample 27), the model is fairly sure of a knee position that's wrong, so that leg snaps briefly. My fix only touches joints below the cutoff, so it doesn't catch this.
